newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan reopens civilian training camps.
newsitem.headline: Sudan reopens civilian training camps.

text.p: Sudan has reopened training camps in Khartoum for civilian volunteers who want to fight alongside the army against Sudanese rebels on the country's eastern border, the government media said on Sunday.
The government-owned al-Sudan al-Hadith newspaper said camps opened in Khartoum on Saturday to train "mujahideen" (holy fighters).
The official news agency SUNA quoted Awad al-Tayeb, deputy coordinator of the Popular Defence Force as saying that 50,000 volunteers had begun training in 150 camps that had opened in Khartoum state.
"The opening of new military training camps comes within the context of the process of preparing to repulse the foreign aggression," Tayeb said.
Sudan accuses Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda of supporting attacks by Sudanese rebels which gained momentum last month in the south and east of Sudan. The three countries deny the charge.
The Popular Defence Force was first set up in 1989 to help government forces crush the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army and other southern rebels in the country's civil war.
